items.title: MemTrial: Learning When to Trust Memory in LLM Portfolio Agents
items.claim: Counterfactual credit for memories, not raw outcomes, keeps LLM portfolio agents within 2.2% of equal-weight on two benchmarks when experience values fail to generalize.

items.title: Beyond Isolation: LLM-Guided Hypergraph Learning across Documents and Horizons for Volatility Prediction from Conference Calls
items.claim: Linking earnings calls across firms through shared LLM-built business-condition factors improves volatility forecasts over 5- to 60-day horizons versus transcript, graph, and financial baselines.

items.title: Consistent But Lenient: Large Language Models Versus Human Underwriters on Borderline Consumer Credit Decisions
items.claim: On borderline credit files, LLM reviewers are more consistent than humans yet approve 79% versus 46%, so consistency alone cannot justify deployment.
